title: Credit Score Factors: What Actually Moves Your FICO
description:
What actually moves your credit score? FICO says a score is built from five parts: payment history 35%, amounts owed 30%, length of credit history 15%, new credit 10% and credit mix 10%. So the biggest wins are paying every bill on time and keeping balances low compared to your limits. Checking your own score does not hurt it.

Sources:
- myFICO, "What's in my FICO Scores?" (factor weights; importance can vary by person), https://www.myfico.com/credit-education/whats-in-your-credit-score (checked 22 Nov 2026)
- myFICO, "Amounts owed" (low utilization helps), https://www.myfico.com/credit-education/credit-scores/amount-of-debt (checked 22 Nov 2026)
- myFICO, "Credit checks and inquiries" (checking your own report doesn't affect your score), https://www.myfico.com/credit-education/credit-reports/credit-checks-and-inquiries (checked 22 Nov 2026)

This covers US FICO Scores; other countries and scoring models differ. The $300-of-$1,000 figure is an example. General education, not financial advice.

scenes.say: One habit makes up thirty-five percent of your credit score. Guess which.
FICO says your score has five parts. They're not equal.
The answer: paying every bill on time. Autopay helps.
Second, thirty percent: amounts owed, like how much of your limits you use.

visual.label: amounts owed
visual.sub: incl. how much of your card limits you use

scenes.say: Three hundred dollars on a one thousand dollar limit: thirty percent. Lower is better.
Now the twist: one thing that feels risky doesn't hurt.
Checking your own score doesn't lower it. Just don't open many cards at once.

visual.title: Quick rules
visual.label: don't apply for many cards at once

scenes.say: Focus on those two: together, almost two-thirds of your score.
